| High caries risk | Every 3–6 months |
| Moderate caries risk | Every 6–12 months |

| Maintenance (post-arrest) | Every 6 months or per caries risk assessment |

| Chitosan | FDA GRAS; non-allergenic; no shellfish protein cross-reactivity; biodegradable |

##### Post-Market Surveillance

- • Ulcerative gingivitis/stomatitis (delay until healing)

The tri-component formulation should be part of a comprehensive caries management program including risk assessment (CAMBRA), dietary counselling, and regular follow-up at 3–6 month intervals.

Advanced Endodontic Solutions

# 3D FLXPOST

Preformed 3D Resin Flex Post

A next-generation prefabricated post manufactured using advanced 3D resin technology — combining CAD-engineered macro-structures with dentin-like flexibility for optimal retention and stress distribution.

CAD-EngineeredDentin-Like ModulusSpiral FlutesSingle-Visit

Add to Cart— ₹500.00 [View Clinical Data](https://sparkdv.com/products/3d-flxpost#clinical-comparison)

![3D FLXPOST Logo](https://sparkdv.com/assets/flxpost-logo-Bt61HyK9.png)

## The Challenge of the Endodontically Treated Tooth

The restoration of endodontically treated teeth (ETT) remains a significant clinical challenge across dental specialties. In both pediatric dentistry — managing primary teeth and traumatized young permanent teeth — and endodontics — restoring mature teeth with compromised structural integrity — the primary goal is the same: to provide coronal retention while preserving radicular dentin and preventing root fractures.

While traditional prefabricated round fiber posts have been the standard for years, they often require aggressive alteration of the natural canal anatomy. The Preformed 3D Resin Flex Post is a next-generation prefabricated solution manufactured using advanced 3D resin technology, offering immediate chairside convenience enhanced by precision CAD-engineered macro-structures.

## What is a Preformed 3D Resin Flex Post?

Unlike standard machined glass fiber posts, preformed 3D resin flex posts are mass-produced using advanced photopolymer resins and 3D manufacturing techniques. The preformed shapes are derived from rigorous Precision CAD (Computer-Aided Design) workflows.

Through advanced inspection and modern 3D viewing tools, engineers validate these designs to ensure they achieve maximum anatomical conformity across diverse canal morphologies before final production.

## Design Architecture

The superiority of the 3D Resin Flex post lies not just in its material, but in its highly engineered surface anatomy.

### Macro-Retention Spiral Flutes

Engineered spiral fluting facilitates optimal hydrodynamic flow and distribution of resin cement during seating, minimizing air voids and maximizing mechanical interlocking between post, cement, and dentin.

### Coronal Support Section

A reinforced, anatomically contoured cervical segment provides robust foundational support for composite core buildup, effectively resisting lateral shear forces and masticatory loads.

### Anatomical Apical Taper

Gradual taper at the apical third mimics the natural convergence of a conservatively prepared root canal, ensuring intimate fit without aggressive, structure-weakening over-enlargement of apical dentin.

### Resin Matrix Flexibility

Proprietary resin composition provides a dentin-like modulus of elasticity, allowing the post to flex symbiotically with the tooth under load.

![3D FLXPOST Design Architecture — Macro-retention Spiral Flutes, Coronal Support Section, Anatomical Apical Taper, Precision CAD](https://sparkdv.com/assets/flxpost-design-architecture-LYIQSNGS.png)

## Anatomical Conformity & Secure Bonding

When evaluating post systems, practitioners must balance structural integrity, tissue preservation, and the quality of the adhesive interface. Because these posts are CAD-optimized for anatomical conformity, the resulting cement layer between the post and the canal wall is exceptionally thin and uniform — reducing the risk of polymerization shrinkage stress, void formation, and eventual debonding.

| Feature | 3D Resin Flex Post | Traditional Round Fiber Post | Cast Metal Post |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Canal Adaptation | Very Good (CAD-optimized anatomical pre-sets) | Fair (Requires modifying oval canals to round) | Excellent (Fully customized) |
| Cement Layer | Thin & Uniform (Aided by spiral flutes) | Variable (Often thick in non-circular canals) | Thin |
| Elastic Modulus | Similar to dentin (~15–20 GPa) | Similar to dentin | Extremely high (Rigid) |
| Root Fracture Risk | Low (Protective stress distribution) | Low to Moderate | High (Wedge effect under load) |

## Clinical Applications

Pediatric Dentistry Endodontics

For the pediatric dentist, chair time and behavioral management are critical. Preformed 3D resin flex posts offer elegant, rapid solutions.

### 1\. Primary Anterior Restorations

Severely decayed primary incisors requiring pulpectomies often lack sufficient coronal tooth structure. Preformed pediatric-sized flex posts provide immediate, robust core support. The coronal support section easily retains a strip crown or zirconia crown, naturally distributing the chewing forces of a growing child.

### 2\. Traumatized Young Permanent Teeth

Teeth with immature apices (blunderbuss canals) are exceptionally fragile. Standard posts are often too narrow for the cervical flare. Preformed 3D posts featuring aggressive coronal tapers can engage the wider cervical areas of young teeth without requiring dangerous removal of the already-thin dentinal walls.

## Clinical Comparison of Endodontic Post Systems

Comprehensive head-to-head evaluation across material composition, biomechanics, workflow, and clinical outcomes.

| Feature | 3D FLXPOST | Prefab Glass Fiber | Prefab Metal | Custom Cast Metal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Material Composition | Advanced CAD-engineered 3D Photopolymer Resin | Woven glass or carbon fibers in epoxy/resin matrix | Titanium alloy or Stainless Steel | Noble or base metal alloys (lab fabricated) |
| Elastic Modulus (Rigidity) | ~15–20 GPa (Closely mimics human dentin) | ~20–40 GPa (Relatively close to dentin) | ~110–200 GPa (Highly rigid) | ~100–200 GPa (Highly rigid) |
| Anatomical Conformity & Fit | High: CAD-optimized pre-sets and anatomical apical taper respect natural canal morphology. | Moderate: Often requires aggressive, circular preparation of oval/ribbon canals. | Low/Moderate: Requires aggressive cylindrical or tapered preparation. | High: Custom-fit via impression. |
| Surface Retention Design | Macro-retention spiral flutes for optimal hydrodynamic cement distribution. | Typically smooth or micro-porous; relies on chemical bonding/friction. | Often threaded or serrated (can induce active stress on root walls). | Smooth or sandblasted surface. |
| Stress Distribution | Evenly distributed; flexes symbiotically with the tooth under load. | Evenly distributed; post typically fails before root fractures. | Concentrated at apex or along threads (active posts). | Concentrated at apex (wedge effect); does not flex. |
| Root Fracture Risk | Low: Protective stress distribution prevents catastrophic failure. | Low to Moderate: Depends on remaining dentin thickness. | Moderate to High: Rigidity increases vertical root fracture risk. | High: Wedge effect frequently leads to vertical root fractures. |
| Clinical Workflow | Single-visit: Select size → Minor prep → Cement | Single-visit: Drill → Fit → Cement | Single-visit: Drill → Fit → Cement | Two-visit: Prep/Impression → Lab fabrication → Cement |
| Retrievability | Excellent: Easily drilled out with standard endodontic burs and ultrasonics. | Good: Drillable, but requires specialized pilot drills. | Moderate: Risk of root fracture during removal. | Poor: Extremely difficult; highest risk of secondary root fracture. |
| Aesthetics / Light Transmission | High: Translucent/tooth-colored; supports light-curing. | High: Excellent light transmission under all-ceramic crowns. | Low: Opaque/metallic; grey shadowing through gingiva. | Low: Opaque/metallic; requires opaque masking. |

## Key Takeaways

### The Dentin-Preservation Advantage

While custom cast posts offer a good fit, they fail in biomechanics (rigidity). Conversely, while fiber posts offer decent biomechanics, they fail in anatomical fit. The 3D FLXPOST bridges this gap by offering both.

### The "Fail-Safe" Mechanism

It is always better for a restoration to fail cohesively (the post debonds or breaks) rather than catastrophically (the root splits). The 3D FLXPOST's dentin-like modulus ensures protective failure modes.

## The 3D FLXPOST Clinical Advantage

The comparative data highlights a critical paradigm shift in post-and-core restorative dentistry. Historically, clinicians have been forced to compromise, choosing between the superior anatomical fit of custom cast posts and the biomechanical safety of prefabricated fiber posts. The 3D FLXPOST system effectively eliminates this compromise.

By combining an elastic modulus that mirrors human dentin with CAD-engineered macro-structures for optimized cement distribution, these preformed posts act symbiotically with the remaining tooth structure rather than acting as a rigid wedge against it. For the pediatric dentist managing a fragile, immature permanent tooth, and the endodontist navigating complex, non-circular canal morphologies, this translates to a highly predictable, single-visit workflow — shifting the clinical focus from simply retaining a core to actively preventing catastrophic root fractures and maximizing dentin preservation.

Clinical Case Documentation

## 3D FLXPOST — Step-by-Step Clinical Case

Sequential clinical documentation of a pediatric anterior rehabilitation using the 3D FLXPOST system — from initial presentation to final aesthetic outcome.

![Case documentation — Pre-Op](https://sparkdv.com/__l5e/assets-v1/044b7f83-2962-4f7b-b510-480640e69309/flxpost-case-preop.png)

Step 1

### Pre-Op

Severely decayed primary incisors with extensive coronal breakdown requiring pulp therapy and post-supported restoration.

![Case documentation — After 3D FLXPOST Application](https://sparkdv.com/__l5e/assets-v1/e631caee-a385-4bc4-971a-31e8301a0fb3/flxpost-case-posts.png)

Step 2

### After 3D FLXPOST Application

Preformed 3D Resin Flex Posts cemented into the prepared canals — CAD-optimized fit with macro-retention spiral flutes visible.

![Case documentation — Core Build-Up](https://sparkdv.com/__l5e/assets-v1/f8769c64-82ad-4cf8-ae81-2e0361f422ee/flxpost-case-core.png)

Step 3

### Core Build-Up

Composite core build-up completed over the flex posts, restoring anatomical form and preparing abutments for definitive crowns.

![Case documentation — After 3D-Resin Crown Placement](https://sparkdv.com/__l5e/assets-v1/4470f73f-003e-4d6a-9b92-8c07db35b3e7/flxpost-case-crown.png)

Step 4

### After 3D-Resin Crown Placement

Final aesthetic outcome after seating of 3D-printed resin crowns — natural translucency, occlusion, and gingival harmony restored.

# ASM — 3D Preformed Resin Bondable Space Maintainer

Digitally engineered arch-space preservation for growing smiles. A modern bonded alternative to the conventional band-and-loop appliance.

[Request Distributor Pricing](https://sparkdv.com/contact) [Book a Demo](https://sparkdv.com/contact)

![ASM — Advanced Space Maintainer, a product of SPARK-DV](https://sparkdv.com/__l5e/assets-v1/2adbe0ff-0160-41db-be8e-6ee3856c90f3/asm-logo.png)

## Overview

The 3D Preformed Resin Pedodontic Bondable Space Maintainer is a digitally designed, additively manufactured fixed appliance built to preserve arch length after early loss of a primary molar. Generated from a parametric digital library and produced through a validated 3D-printing workflow, each unit ships pre-shaped to standard pediatric arch dimensions — ready for direct chairside bonding, without the wire-bending, band fitting, or soldering steps required by conventional band-and-loop appliances.

Why It Matters

## Unmanaged space loss follows a predictable path

Once a primary molar is lost early, the surrounding dentition does not wait for the permanent successor — space is lost on a timeline, not a threshold.

1. 01


### Tooth Lost


Primary molar extracted or exfoliates prematurely; socket begins to remodel.

2. 02


### Adjacent Drift


Mesial tooth tips into the space within weeks; arch length begins to shrink.

3. 03


### Opposing Extrusion


The unopposed tooth super-erupts, complicating future occlusion.

4. 04


### Arch Length Loss


Available space for the permanent successor is measurably reduced.

5. 05


### Eruption Complications


Impaction, ectopic eruption, or crowding become more likely without intervention.


Chairside to Delivery

## A four-step digital workflow

Preformed geometry replaces the impression-to-lab-solder cycle with a scan-to-bond sequence.

01

### Scan

Intraoral scan captures the edentulous span and abutment tooth contours.

02

### Select / Design

Closest span size is selected from the parametric library — arch- and side-matched.

03

### Print

Appliance is additively manufactured and validated for manifold, watertight geometry.

04

### Bond

Delivered chairside using standard etch-and-bond protocol — no soldering step.

Appliance Anatomy

## Bonded in place of a band — not in place of judgment

### Bonded Resin Pad

Etched & bonded to abutment.

### Edentulous Span

Matched to library size.

### Contoured Spacer Bar

Arch-curvature matched, preformed.

### Preformed Contact

Seats against the mesial tooth.

Geometry mirrors across arch and side variants in the digital library.

## Key Features

### Digitally Designed

For pediatric arch morphology, with arch-specific (maxillary/mandibular) and side-specific (left/right) curvature.

### Preformed Resin Body

Fast try-in and chairside adaptation — no soldering or wire-loop fabrication.

### Bondable Interface

Simplifies placement using standard orthodontic/restorative bonding protocols.

### Sized Library Coverage

A range of mesiodistal spans matches tooth-to-tooth spacing without custom fabrication delays.

### Print-Validated Geometry

Manifold and dimensionally accurate for a consistent, repeatable fit.

### Streamlined Digital Workflow

Compatible with intraoral scan–to–appliance pipelines.

## Clinical Advantages

Early loss of a primary molar allows adjacent and opposing teeth to drift, reducing the space available for the permanent successor. Fixed space maintainers counter this by holding the mesiodistal width of the edentulous span until the permanent tooth is ready to erupt.

- ### Reduced Chair Time



No impression-model soldering cycle; the appliance arrives pre-shaped to the selected span size.

- ### Improved Fit Prediction



Parametric sizing across multiple span increments allows closer matching to the actual edentulous gap.

- ### Simplified Bonding Sequence



A bondable base integrates with conventional adhesive protocols rather than crimped or soldered bands.

- ### Consistent, Repeatable Geometry



Every unit is generated from validated digital files, reducing operator-dependent variability.


## Important Considerations

As with any fixed pediatric appliance, long-term clinical success depends on more than the appliance itself:

### Retention is the primary variable to manage.

Evaluate bonded resin interfaces for adhesive protocol, isolation, and moisture control at placement. Check appliances at recall visits for early signs of debonding.

### Oral hygiene reinforcement is essential.

Fixed space maintainers — bonded or banded — can increase plaque accumulation around the abutment tooth if hygiene is not reinforced. Provide clear home-care instructions.

### Appliance selection should match the clinical picture.

Assess span size, abutment tooth condition, and opposing occlusion before selecting a size from the library.

## Sizing & Fit

Available across a range of mesiodistal span sizes, covering both maxillary and mandibular arches and both left and right sides. Clinicians select the closest match to the measured edentulous space rather than adapting a one-size appliance chairside.

8.5 mm9.5 mm10.5 mm11.5 mmMaxillaryMandibularLeftRight

Indicative span library — please confirm sizes with your distributor.

## Suitable For

- Early/premature loss of a primary molar
- Pediatric patients requiring fixed (non-removable) space maintenance
- Practices with intraoral scanning and digital workflow capability
- Chairside or lab-based additive manufacturing protocols

## Preformed Resin vs. Conventional Band-and-Loop

|  | 3D Preformed Resin Bondable | Conventional Band-and-Loop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fabrication | Digitally designed, additively manufactured, preformed | Hand-fitted band + hand-bent/soldered wire loop |
| Chair Time | Reduced — pre-shaped for direct bonding | Longer — impression, lab soldering, try-in |
| Fit Method | Selected from sized digital library | Adjusted/crimped chairside or at lab |
| Attachment | Bonded resin interface | Cemented band |
| Operator Variability | Lower — standardized digital geometry | Higher — manual bending/soldering |
| Key Limitation | Bond retention over time | Band decementation, solder joint failure |

Digitally designed for precision, comfort, and pediatric efficiency — a modern bonded space-maintaining solution for growing smiles.

## Enhanced Clinical Advantages

#### Superior Strength + Flexibility

Black Gold & Black Oxide NiTi deliver higher flexibility and cyclic fatigue resistance than conventional austenitic NiTi. Thermo-mechanical treatment increases martensite/R-phase content at body temperature for safer negotiation of curved, narrow and calcified canals.

#### High Cutting Efficiency

Oxide surface layer and optimized cross-sections maintain cutting efficiency despite greater flexibility — faster canal preparation with fewer procedural errors such as ledging, zipping and perforation.

#### Non-Cutting Tip

Rounded, non-cutting tips provide safer apical progression and reduced risk of apical transportation or perforation — especially valuable in the delicate anatomy of primary teeth.

#### Excellent Debris Removal

S-shaped (single-file) and triangular (3-file) cross-sections promote efficient coronal debris extrusion and better irrigation flow, resulting in cleaner canal walls.

#### Ideal for Narrow & Calcified Canals

Enhanced flexibility with controlled memory-like behaviour allows better centering and progressive enlargement while preserving more dentin in constricted pediatric canals.

#### Purpose-Designed for Pediatrics

Shorter overall lengths (17–19 mm) and working lengths (12–13 mm) match primary tooth roots, reducing over-instrumentation risk and improving patient comfort through shorter chair time.

## Black Oxide NiTi — The Science

Safer, stronger, smarter performance through surface engineering and controlled phase transformation.

#### Black Oxide (TiO₂)

Enhances corrosion resistance and reduces surface friction.

#### Black Gold (TiN)

Increases surface hardness and wear resistance for prolonged cutting efficiency.

#### NiTi Core

Provides flexibility and cyclic fatigue resistance.

#### Optimized Phase Transformation

Surface treatment and controlled heat activation optimize martensite–austenite phase behaviour at clinical temperatures (≈34–37 °C), enabling controlled flexibility inside the canal and superior shape memory for efficient recovery with reduced risk of distortion or separation.

# Science & Research

Our products are built on a foundation of rigorous scientific research and clinical validation. Explore the science behind Spark DV.

## How Our Technology Works

Understanding the mechanisms behind NanoSilver Fluoride's effectiveness in caries prevention.

### Antibacterial Action

NanoSilver particles (10-20nm) disrupt bacterial cell membranes through multiple mechanisms, reducing the population of acid-producing bacteria that cause caries.

Silver nanoparticles interact with bacterial cell walls, causing structural damage and interfering with respiratory enzymes.

![NSF Antibacterial Mechanism Diagram](https://sparkdv.com/assets/nsf-antibacterial-diagram-Dp4Pyfpy.png)

### Biofilm Disruption

Our nano-sized particles penetrate the extracellular matrix of dental biofilm, disrupting its protective structure.

This allows better penetration of antimicrobial and remineralizing agents to the tooth surface.

![NSF Biofilm Disruption Mechanism Diagram](https://sparkdv.com/assets/nsf-biofilm-diagram-LxLNoosV.png)

### Remineralization Support

Fluoride ions and nano-hydroxyapatite work synergistically to deposit minerals into demineralized enamel.

Nano-hydroxyapatite provides a reservoir of calcium and phosphate ions that support natural remineralization processes.

![NSF Remineralization Mechanism Diagram](https://sparkdv.com/assets/nsf-remineralization-diagram-wFf-cVns.png)

Clinical Evidence

## Evidence Library

Access our collection of peer-reviewed studies and clinical research supporting our products.

### NanoSilver Fluoride Technology

12 Published Studies

Peer-reviewed research on the efficacy and safety of our patented NanoSilver Fluoride compounds.

View Studies

### Non-Staining Formulations

5 Published Studies

Studies comparing staining potential versus traditional silver diamine fluoride treatments.

View Studies

### Pediatric Applications

8 Published Studies

Clinical evidence for use in early childhood caries prevention and management.

View Studies

### Bioactive Materials

6 Published Studies

Research on bioactive glass and nano-calcium compounds for pulp therapy and restoration.

View Studies

[Request Full Research Package](https://sparkdv.com/contact)

## Safety & Non-Staining Technology

One of the key advantages of our NanoSilver Fluoride technology over traditional silver diamine fluoride (SDF) is our formulation designed to minimize staining.

Traditional SDF treatments often result in black staining of arrested carious lesions, which can be cosmetically unacceptable for many patients. Our patented formulation addresses this concern through stabilized nanosilver particles and optimized delivery systems.

#### Clinical Note

While our products are formulated to be non-staining compared to in-office SDF treatments, individual results may vary. Consult with a dental professional for personalized recommendations.

### Non-Staining Formula

Designed for patient acceptance and aesthetic outcomes

Our Founder

## Dr. Ajay Reddy Mareddy

Founder and Managing Director of SPARK-DV, where science, clinical insight, and product innovation come together to redefine preventive dentistry.

A practicing dentist and academic researcher, he has spent years working at the intersection of patient care, dental biomaterials, and minimally invasive treatment approaches.

His innovation journey is reflected in publicly available WIPO patent publications, including WO2009098710A1 (Formocresol gel) and WO2015155629A1 (Saturation method of a drug for dental). These filings focused on improving dental materials and delivery systems through safer formulations, better clinical handling, and biomaterial-based approaches such as PLGA-assisted obturation and controlled therapeutic release.

Alongside this patent work, Dr. Mareddy has continued to publish research in pediatric and preventive dentistry, including recent PubMed-indexed studies on nanosilver fluoride, silver diamine fluoride, dental sealants, and remineralization-focused care. SPARK-DV builds on that foundation: products shaped not by marketing first, but by decades of clinical observation, formulation research, and evidence-led development.

# For Parents

Simple, clear information to help you make the best oral care decisions for your family. Because every smile deserves protection.

## What Causes Cavities?

Cavities form when bacteria in the mouth produce acids that dissolve tooth enamel. Sugary foods and drinks, poor brushing habits, and certain medical conditions can increase cavity risk.

Children with braces, frequent snacking habits, or a history of cavities are at higher risk and may benefit from advanced preventive care.

![Caries Causing Agents - Sugary Foods, Bacteria, Plaque, Poor Hygiene](https://sparkdv.com/assets/caries-causing-agents-ash5odDj.png)

## What Are White Spots?

White spots on teeth are early signs of enamel demineralization — the first stage before a cavity forms. They're common in children with braces or poor oral hygiene.

Early intervention with remineralizing products can help support the natural repair process before more serious damage occurs.

![White spots on teeth - early signs of enamel demineralization](https://sparkdv.com/assets/white-spots-teeth-BQXHGZg8.png)

## How to Brush Correctly

1

Use a pea-sized amount of toothpaste on a soft-bristled brush.

2

Brush gently in small circular motions for 2 full minutes.

3

Cover all surfaces: outer, inner, and chewing surfaces.

4

Spit out thoroughly — do NOT rinse with water (for best protection).

5

Avoid eating or drinking for 30 minutes after brushing.

6

Brush twice daily: morning and before bed.

## Which Product is Right?

### Nanion Lite

Best for everyday prevention — your child has moderate risk or you want daily advanced protection.

- ✓ Daily home use
- ✓ Ages 6+ with supervision
- ✓ General preventive care

[Learn More](https://sparkdv.com/products/nanion-lite)

### Nanion Elite

Best for higher-risk situations — braces, frequent cavities, or your dentist recommends stronger protection.

- ✓ Higher concentration formula
- ✓ Orthodontic / high-risk patients
- ✓ Use under dentist guidance

[Learn More](https://sparkdv.com/products/nanion-elite)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is NanoSilver Fluoride safe for children?

Our products are formulated with pediatric safety in mind. Nanion Lite is designed for ages 6+ with adult supervision. Always follow the recommended usage and consult your dentist.

### Will it stain my child's teeth?

Our formulations are designed to be non-staining compared to in-office SDF treatments. Individual results may vary.

### What if my child swallows the toothpaste?

Use only a pea-sized amount. Spit out after brushing. If a small amount is accidentally swallowed, it is generally not harmful, but consult your dentist if concerned.

### At what age can my child start using Nanion products?

Nanion Lite is recommended for ages 6 and above with adult supervision. For younger children, consult your pediatric dentist for personalized guidance.

### Can it help with sensitivity?

Our formulations include ingredients that support enamel health, which may help with sensitivity. Consult your dentist for persistent sensitivity issues.

### Is Nanion Swish safe for children?

Nanion Swish can be used by children who can reliably spit (typically 6+). Always supervise and ensure the child does not swallow the rinse.

**Disclaimer:** The information on this page is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional dental consultation. Always consult your child's dentist for personalized recommendations.

## Have More Questions?

Our team is happy to help you find the right products for your family.

## Nanion Lite Pro vs Elite Pro

[**Nanion Lite Pro** \\
2% NSF + 5% Nano-Hydroxyapatite\\
\\

THE PRO UPGRADE

## Why Standard NSF Alone Is Not the Ceiling

Standard Nanion addresses bacterial persistence, biofilm impermeability, and short fluoride release. But a fourth dimension remains: physical structural integrity of enamel and dentinal tubule management.

#### Surface Architecture Gap

White spot lesions have an intact but porous surface layer. Standard NSF provides ionic remineralisation but not physical particulate deposit at the surface layer to restore crystallographic continuity and optical homogeneity.

#### Dentinal Tubule Exposure

Exposed dentinal tubules (1–2.5 µm diameter) allow hydrodynamic fluid movement activating A-δ nerve fibres. Conventional NSF does not directly occlude these tubules. nHA is an ideal tubule-occluding agent.

#### Compositional Identity

Hydroxyapatite \[Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂\] is 96 wt% of human enamel. nHA is structurally and chemically identical to biologic enamel apatite, enabling thermodynamically favourable adsorption onto demineralised surfaces.

#### Sequential Synergy

NSF's chitosan disrupts the EPS biofilm matrix, clearing the enamel surface of plaque — creating ideal contact conditions for nHA adsorption. The two systems are mechanistically sequential: NSF prepares; nHA deposits.

DUAL-MATRIX TECHNOLOGY

## Four-Action PRO Mechanism

Each action enhances the conditions for the next. A sequential cascade creating synergistic outcomes that neither NSF alone nor nHA alone can produce.

1

#### Kill

Antibacterial Destruction

5–8 nm AgNPs pierce bacterial membranes, generate ROS, inhibit NADH dehydrogenase and DNA topoisomerase II.

≥4× lower MIC vs. NaF

2

#### Disrupt

Biofilm Matrix Breakdown

Cationic chitosan destabilises the EPS matrix, creating channels for silver, fluoride, and nHA to access sub-surface enamel.

>70% biofilm reduction

3

#### Rebuild

Sustained F⁻ Release

Chitosan polymer forms a slow-release F⁻ depot. Fluoride integrates into the crystal lattice forming fluorapatite.

12hr sustained release

4

PRO ONLY

#### Repair

nHA Biomimetic Repair

5% nHA particles deposit onto demineralised surfaces and physically occlude dentinal tubules. Dual remineralisation cascade.

78% tubule occlusion

#### Why Sequential Order Matters

In a standalone nHA toothpaste applied over intact dental plaque, the EPS matrix acts as a physical barrier — nHA particles cannot contact the enamel surface. In Nanion Pro, chitosan first disrupts the EPS matrix (Action 2), creating channels for nHA to reach the enamel directly. Simultaneously, the bactericidal action (Action 1) reduces the acid-producing load, creating an alkaline microenvironment favourable to hydroxyapatite precipitation (critical pH ~5.5 for enamel).

5% NANO-HYDROXYAPATITE

## Why 5% nHA Is the Optimal Concentration

Efficacy Threshold

Published literature demonstrates meaningful enamel remineralisation and tubule occlusion at 5–10%. At 5%, Pro achieves the clinically validated threshold without particle aggregation that reduces bioavailability.

Colloidal Stability

The chitosan carrier that stabilises 5–8 nm AgNPs also provides a colloidal environment compatible with nHA suspension. At 5%, nHA does not disrupt the chitosan-silver stabilisation mechanism.

Paediatric Safety Margin

At 5%, the calcium phosphate load from incidental ingestion is physiologically negligible and well within accepted safe ingestion limits for calcium and phosphate.

### New Clinical Capabilities Unlocked by 5% nHA

Physical surface reconstruction of WSLs — not just ionic remineralisation

Dentinal tubule occlusion for hypersensitivity — relevant in primary teeth with wide, open tubules

Pre-conditioning of enamel for enhanced fluoride uptake — nHA-deposited Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻ increase local ion availability

Protection during low-pH events — nHA acts as a calcium-phosphate buffer, sacrificially dissolving to mitigate acid-induced mineral loss

CLINICAL SCENARIOS

## The nHA Advantage in Practice

Four clinical scenarios where the PRO dual-matrix delivers differentiated outcomes

#### Active WSL Management — Orthodontics

Bracket-adjacent WSLs are inaccessible to mechanical debridement. Chitosan disrupts plaque at bracket margins; AgNPs reduce S. mutans; fluoride remineralises the subsurface body; nHA physically deposits on the surface, restoring mineral density and optical appearance.

#### ECC with Dentinal Involvement

Primary teeth have wider, more permeable dentinal tubules. Elite Pro provides the most potent at-home caries-arresting regimen: bactericidal action + biofilm disruption + sustained F⁻ + nHA tubule sealing to reduce sensitivity and slow pulpal bacterial penetration.

#### Post-Dietary-Erosion Sensitivity

Patients with high acidic beverage intake present with widely patent dentinal tubules and thinned enamel. Lite Pro provides nHA-mediated tubule occlusion for sensitivity while NSF manages the associated cariogenic biofilm — a dual benefit unavailable from either agent alone.

#### Post-Scaling Sensitivity

Paediatric patients undergoing full-mouth debridement may experience transient dentinal hypersensitivity. Pro provides post-scaling sensitivity management that simultaneously maintains caries prevention — a dual-purpose prescription in a single product.

TECHNOLOGY COMPARISON

## PRO vs. Alternatives

| Parameter | Lite Pro | Elite Pro | Conv. NaF | Standalone nHA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active Ingredients | AgNPs + Chitosan + F⁻ + 5% nHA | AgNPs + Chitosan + F⁻ + 5% nHA | NaF only | nHA only |
| NSF Concentration | 2% (Lite) | 3% (Elite) | — | — |
| Direct Antibacterial | ✔ Potent | ✔ Potent | ✖ Indirect | ✖ None |
| Biofilm Disruption | ✔ Strong | ✔ Strong | ✖ None | ⚠ Minimal |
| WSL Arrest | ✔ 89% | ✔ 89%+ | ✖ Minimal | ⚠ Early only |
| Dentinal Arrest | ✔ 85% | ✔ 85%+ | ✖ None | ✖ None |
| Tubule Occlusion | ✔ nHA | ✔ nHA | ✖ None | ✔ Primary use |
| Sub-surface Remin. | ✔ NSF + nHA surface | ✔ Full-depth | ✖ Surface only | ⚠ Surface only |
| F⁻ Release | Up to 12 hrs | Up to 12 hrs | 2–4 hrs | None |
| Sensitivity Relief | ✔ nHA occlusion | ✔ nHA occlusion | ✖ None | ✔ Primary use |
| Staining | ✔ None | ✔ None | ✔ None | ✔ None |
| Primary Indication | Mod–high risk + sensitivity | ECC, xerostomia, active decay | Low-risk maintenance | Sensitivity only |

The addition of 5% nHA does not reduce NSF's antibacterial or biofilm-disrupting potency. The nHA and NSF components operate on different substrates and do not competitively inhibit one another.

PEER-REVIEWED EVIDENCE

## Clinical Evidence Base

Dual evidence streams: NSF (Studies 1–3) and nano-hydroxyapatite (Studies 4–5)

Journal of Dentistry

Double-Blind RCT · 18 months

89% reduction in WSL progression vs. standard NaF

Quantitative light-induced fluorescence (QLF); subsurface mineral loss as primary endpoint; 67% lesion regression in NSF group.

Frontiers in Bioengineering

Biofilm Reactor · MIC Study

4× lower MIC than NaF; >70% biofilm biomass reduction

Validated against mature S. mutans biofilms using crystal violet staining and CFU counts.

BMC Oral Health

Primary Dentition RCT

85% arrest of active dentinal caries in primary teeth

Vickers microhardness confirmed measurable hardening of previously leathery carious dentine. Only OTC-format agent with published dentinal arrest data.

nHA EVIDENCE

Journal of Clinical Dentistry / Caries Research

nHA Remineralisation RCT

nHA achieves equivalent or superior enamel remineralisation to 1,450 ppm NaF

Superior optical lesion regression on artificial WSL specimens. nHA's surface-layer mineralisation complemented fluoride's subsurface remineralisation for greater total mineral recovery.

nHA EVIDENCE

Clinical Oral Investigations

nHA Tubule Occlusion · SEM Study

78% complete dentinal tubule occlusion after 2-week protocol

SEM confirmed occlusion maintained under simulated acid challenge (pH 4.5, 5-minute exposure). Attributed to crystallographic integration of nHA into peritubular dentine matrix.

PATIENT SELECTION

## Who Benefits Most from the PRO Line

Patients who derive the greatest marginal benefit from upgrading to dual-matrix over standard NSF

### Nanion Lite Pro Indications

### Moderate Caries Risk + Sensitivity

### Orthodontic Prophylaxis (Pre-WSL)

### Nanion Elite Pro Indications

### High-Risk ECC — First-Line Agent

### Established Bracket-Adjacent WSLs

### Xerostomia / Medically Compromised

### Fluoride-Resistant Biofilm

### Active Dentinal Caries — Deferred Treatment

APPLICATION PROTOCOL

## Optimised PRO Line Protocol

The no-rinse protocol is non-negotiable for realising the full 12-hour F⁻ reservoir and nHA adsorption window

1

Apply pea-sized amount to a DRY toothbrush

Dry bristles maximise particle-enamel contact; prevents premature dilution of the NSF-nHA colloidal matrix before surface adsorption.

2

Brush all surfaces systematically — 2 minutes minimum

Full dentition coverage; mechanical activation of chitosan-EPS interaction; distributes nHA to all enamel surfaces including bracket-enamel interfaces.

3

Expectorate thoroughly. DO NOT rinse with water

Critical: rinsing removes the NSF-nHA film and eliminates the 12-hour sustained-release F⁻ reservoir and nHA adsorption window.

4

No food or drink for 30 minutes post-brushing

Allows nHA particle integration into enamel pores and nascent WSL surface; allows chitosan-F⁻ depot to establish sustained-release kinetics.

5

Targeted fingertip application to active WSLs or hypersensitive zones

Leave-on application maximises WSL arrest potential; direct nHA tubule occlusion in hypersensitive areas without further mechanical disturbance.

#### Age-Specific Dosing — PRO Line

- • Ages 6–12: Pea-sized amount (~0.5 g), caregiver-supervised. Explicit instruction on spitting without rinsing — model the behaviour with caregivers at the chair.
- • Ages 3–5 (Elite Pro, high ECC risk): Smear-sized amount (~0.25 g), fully caregiver-applied. nHA is compositionally safe; NSF is non-bioavailable in rinse-off format at smear doses.
- • Orthodontic (all ages): Standard pea-sized dose + fingertip application to bracket-enamel interfaces. Wipe excess from bracket surfaces with dry gauze; do not rinse.
- • Xerostomic: Twice-daily Elite Pro plus mid-day low-dose fingertip application to most at-risk areas, in consultation with managing physician.

CAMBRA-ALIGNED PROTOCOL

## Risk-Stratified Integration Protocol

PRO line positioned within a comprehensive paediatric caries management framework

| Risk Category | Recommended PRO Formula | Professional Adjuncts | Recall & Monitoring |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Low Risk | Conventional NaF (PRO not required) | Fluoride varnish 6-monthly | Annual; CAMBRA re-stratification |
| Moderate Risk | Nanion Lite Pro (2% NSF + 5% nHA) twice daily | Varnish quarterly; dietary review; sealants | 6-monthly; QLF / ICDAS scoring |
| High Risk / ECC | Nanion Elite Pro (3% NSF + 5% nHA) — first-line | SDF 38% for cavitated; varnish quarterly; xylitol programme | 3-monthly; ICDAS, microhardness monitoring |
| Ortho / WSL | Elite Pro + targeted WSL fingertip application | Varnish at each ortho check-up; CPP-ACP adjunct | Each appointment; photo documentation |
| Xerostomia | Elite Pro — first-line (compensates absent saliva) | Saliva substitutes; xylitol lozenges; varnish monthly | Monthly during episode; 3-monthly otherwise |
| Sensitivity + Caries | Lite Pro or Elite Pro (nHA provides tubule occlusion) | Avoid SDF if aesthetics priority; CPP-ACP for Ca²⁺ | 6–8 weeks for sensitivity; NRS pain scale |

CAREGIVER EDUCATION

## Chair-Side Communication Framework

Clinical outcomes are heavily dependent on correct caregiver technique

#### Why no rinsing?

"This toothpaste contains two special ingredients — tiny silver particles that fight cavity-causing bacteria, and nano-hydroxyapatite, which is exactly the same material as your child's own tooth enamel. If you rinse, you wash these away before they have a chance to work. The protective film works for up to 12 hours. Spitting without rinsing is the most important thing you can do."

#### Why fingertip application to white spots?

"These white marks are early cavities forming under the surface. Putting a small amount directly on them with a clean finger — and leaving it there — allows the nano-hydroxyapatite to fill in porous areas and the silver to stop the bacteria making them worse. This is the equivalent of giving the tooth a direct treatment every day at home."

#### Is the silver safe?

"Yes. The silver is encapsulated — held in a protective shell that only releases where it needs to work, on the bacterial cells causing decay. It does not absorb into the body and won't stain the teeth black like some silver treatments applied in the clinic."

#### How is this different from regular toothpaste?

"Regular toothpaste leaves a protective layer on the outside. This toothpaste does that too, but it also kills the bacteria causing the cavity, breaks down the plaque shield, and fills in the early cavity from both inside and outside simultaneously. For a child with cavity history, this covers all four ways we need to protect the teeth."

## Safety Profile — PRO Dual-Matrix

### nHA Safety: Systemic and Local

Nano-hydroxyapatite is compositionally identical to the body's own bone and tooth mineral. It is non-cytotoxic at dentifrice concentrations, does not accumulate systemically (metabolised via normal calcium and phosphate pathways), and does not stain teeth, gingiva, or restorations. For paediatric patients, the nHA component raises no additional safety concerns.

### No Tooth Staining — Unlike SDF

SDF's black staining arises from free Ag⁺ reduction by sulphur-containing proteins in carious dentine. In Nanion Pro, AgNPs are chitosan-stabilised and do not release free Ag⁺ at concentrations sufficient to cause this reaction. Pro can be recommended for anterior teeth and aesthetically sensitive sites without the staining caveat that limits SDF use.

### Systemic Silver Safety in PRO Context

The addition of nHA does not alter the silver nanoparticle safety profile. Chitosan stabilisation of 5–8 nm AgNPs maintains colloidal structure preventing free ionic silver dissociation. Nanion Pro remains a rinse-off topical product with negligible systemic AgNP bioavailability.

### Safety & Caution

- • For ages 6 and above. Use under adult supervision for children.
- • Children 3–5: Elite Pro only under dentist guidance in confirmed high-ECC-risk cases.
- • Do not swallow. Keep out of reach of children.
- • Discontinue use if irritation occurs and consult a dentist.
- • Not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.

**Regulatory & Professional Disclaimer:** Nanion Lite Pro and Nanion Elite Pro are advanced dental hygiene products classified as OTC anti-caries products, indicated for the prevention of dental caries and enamel remineralisation. The nano-hydroxyapatite component is included as a biocompatible remineralising and desensitising agent. Claims presented reflect conclusions from published peer-reviewed research and have not been independently evaluated by the FDA as specific disease treatments or cures. This content is prepared for qualified dental professionals for educational purposes only and does not constitute a prescription or clinical directive. Individual patient assessment, clinical judgement, and reference to current evidence-based guidelines remain the practitioner's responsibility. Always consult current AAPD, EAPD, and CAMBRA guidelines when implementing paediatric caries prevention protocols. © 2026 Nanion.in. All rights reserved. US Patent Protected.

THE PRO UPGRADE

## Why Standard NSF Alone Is Not the Ceiling

Standard Nanion addresses bacterial persistence, biofilm impermeability, and short fluoride release. But a fourth dimension remains: physical structural integrity of enamel and dentinal tubule management.

#### Surface Architecture Gap

White spot lesions have an intact but porous surface layer. Standard NSF provides ionic remineralisation but not physical particulate deposit at the surface layer to restore crystallographic continuity and optical homogeneity.

#### Dentinal Tubule Exposure

Exposed dentinal tubules (1–2.5 µm diameter) allow hydrodynamic fluid movement activating A-δ nerve fibres. Conventional NSF does not directly occlude these tubules. nHA is an ideal tubule-occluding agent.

#### Compositional Identity

Hydroxyapatite \[Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂\] is 96 wt% of human enamel. nHA is structurally and chemically identical to biologic enamel apatite, enabling thermodynamically favourable adsorption onto demineralised surfaces.

#### Sequential Synergy

NSF's chitosan disrupts the EPS biofilm matrix, clearing the enamel surface of plaque — creating ideal contact conditions for nHA adsorption. The two systems are mechanistically sequential: NSF prepares; nHA deposits.

DUAL-MATRIX TECHNOLOGY

## Four-Action PRO Mechanism

Each action enhances the conditions for the next. A sequential cascade creating synergistic outcomes that neither NSF alone nor nHA alone can produce.

1

#### Kill

Antibacterial Destruction

5–8 nm AgNPs pierce bacterial membranes, generate ROS, inhibit NADH dehydrogenase and DNA topoisomerase II.

≥4× lower MIC vs. NaF

2

#### Disrupt

Biofilm Matrix Breakdown

Cationic chitosan destabilises the EPS matrix, creating channels for silver, fluoride, and nHA to access sub-surface enamel.

>70% biofilm reduction

3

#### Rebuild

Sustained F⁻ Release

Chitosan polymer forms a slow-release F⁻ depot. Fluoride integrates into the crystal lattice forming fluorapatite.

12hr sustained release

4

PRO ONLY

#### Repair

nHA Biomimetic Repair

5% nHA particles deposit onto demineralised surfaces and physically occlude dentinal tubules. Dual remineralisation cascade.

78% tubule occlusion

#### Why Sequential Order Matters

In a standalone nHA toothpaste applied over intact dental plaque, the EPS matrix acts as a physical barrier — nHA particles cannot contact the enamel surface. In Nanion Pro, chitosan first disrupts the EPS matrix (Action 2), creating channels for nHA to reach the enamel directly. Simultaneously, the bactericidal action (Action 1) reduces the acid-producing load, creating an alkaline microenvironment favourable to hydroxyapatite precipitation (critical pH ~5.5 for enamel).

5% NANO-HYDROXYAPATITE

## Why 5% nHA Is the Optimal Concentration

Efficacy Threshold

Published literature demonstrates meaningful enamel remineralisation and tubule occlusion at 5–10%. At 5%, Pro achieves the clinically validated threshold without particle aggregation that reduces bioavailability.

Colloidal Stability

The chitosan carrier that stabilises 5–8 nm AgNPs also provides a colloidal environment compatible with nHA suspension. At 5%, nHA does not disrupt the chitosan-silver stabilisation mechanism.

Paediatric Safety Margin

At 5%, the calcium phosphate load from incidental ingestion is physiologically negligible and well within accepted safe ingestion limits for calcium and phosphate.

### New Clinical Capabilities Unlocked by 5% nHA

Physical surface reconstruction of WSLs — not just ionic remineralisation

Dentinal tubule occlusion for hypersensitivity — relevant in primary teeth with wide, open tubules

Pre-conditioning of enamel for enhanced fluoride uptake — nHA-deposited Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻ increase local ion availability

Protection during low-pH events — nHA acts as a calcium-phosphate buffer, sacrificially dissolving to mitigate acid-induced mineral loss

CLINICAL SCENARIOS

## The nHA Advantage in Practice

Four clinical scenarios where the PRO dual-matrix delivers differentiated outcomes

#### Active WSL Management — Orthodontics

Bracket-adjacent WSLs are inaccessible to mechanical debridement. Chitosan disrupts plaque at bracket margins; AgNPs reduce S. mutans; fluoride remineralises the subsurface body; nHA physically deposits on the surface, restoring mineral density and optical appearance.

#### ECC with Dentinal Involvement

Primary teeth have wider, more permeable dentinal tubules. Elite Pro provides the most potent at-home caries-arresting regimen: bactericidal action + biofilm disruption + sustained F⁻ + nHA tubule sealing to reduce sensitivity and slow pulpal bacterial penetration.

#### Post-Dietary-Erosion Sensitivity

Patients with high acidic beverage intake present with widely patent dentinal tubules and thinned enamel. Lite Pro provides nHA-mediated tubule occlusion for sensitivity while NSF manages the associated cariogenic biofilm — a dual benefit unavailable from either agent alone.

#### Post-Scaling Sensitivity

Paediatric patients undergoing full-mouth debridement may experience transient dentinal hypersensitivity. Pro provides post-scaling sensitivity management that simultaneously maintains caries prevention — a dual-purpose prescription in a single product.

PEER-REVIEWED EVIDENCE

## Clinical Evidence Base

Dual evidence streams: NSF (Studies 1–3) and nano-hydroxyapatite (Studies 4–5)

Double-Blind RCT · 18 months

89% reduction in WSL progression vs. standard NaF

Quantitative light-induced fluorescence (QLF); subsurface mineral loss as primary endpoint; 67% lesion regression in NSF group.

4× lower MIC than NaF; >70% biofilm biomass reduction

Validated against mature S. mutans biofilms using crystal violet staining and CFU counts.

BMC Oral Health

Primary Dentition RCT

85% arrest of active dentinal caries in primary teeth

Vickers microhardness confirmed measurable hardening of previously leathery carious dentine. Only OTC-format agent with published dentinal arrest data.

nHA EVIDENCE

nHA Remineralisation RCT

nHA achieves equivalent or superior enamel remineralisation to 1,450 ppm NaF

Superior optical lesion regression on artificial WSL specimens. nHA's surface-layer mineralisation complemented fluoride's subsurface remineralisation for greater total mineral recovery.

78% complete dentinal tubule occlusion after 2-week protocol

APPLICATION PROTOCOL

## Optimised PRO Line Protocol

The no-rinse protocol is non-negotiable for realising the full 12-hour F⁻ reservoir and nHA adsorption window

1

Apply pea-sized amount to a DRY toothbrush

Dry bristles maximise particle-enamel contact; prevents premature dilution of the NSF-nHA colloidal matrix before surface adsorption.

2

Brush all surfaces systematically — 2 minutes minimum

Full dentition coverage; mechanical activation of chitosan-EPS interaction; distributes nHA to all enamel surfaces including bracket-enamel interfaces.

3

Expectorate thoroughly. DO NOT rinse with water

Critical: rinsing removes the NSF-nHA film and eliminates the 12-hour sustained-release F⁻ reservoir and nHA adsorption window.

4

No food or drink for 30 minutes post-brushing

Allows nHA particle integration into enamel pores and nascent WSL surface; allows chitosan-F⁻ depot to establish sustained-release kinetics.

5

Targeted fingertip application to active WSLs or hypersensitive zones

Leave-on application maximises WSL arrest potential; direct nHA tubule occlusion in hypersensitive areas without further mechanical disturbance.

#### Age-Specific Dosing — PRO Line

- • Ages 6–12: Pea-sized amount (~0.5 g), caregiver-supervised. Explicit instruction on spitting without rinsing — model the behaviour with caregivers at the chair.
- • Ages 3–5 (Elite Pro, high ECC risk): Smear-sized amount (~0.25 g), fully caregiver-applied. nHA is compositionally safe; NSF is non-bioavailable in rinse-off format at smear doses.
- • Orthodontic (all ages): Standard pea-sized dose + fingertip application to bracket-enamel interfaces. Wipe excess from bracket surfaces with dry gauze; do not rinse.
- • Xerostomic: Twice-daily Elite Pro plus mid-day low-dose fingertip application to most at-risk areas, in consultation with managing physician.

CAMBRA-ALIGNED PROTOCOL

## Risk-Stratified Integration Protocol

PRO line positioned within a comprehensive paediatric caries management framework

| Low Risk | Conventional NaF (PRO not required) | Fluoride varnish 6-monthly | Annual; CAMBRA re-stratification |
| Moderate Risk | Nanion Lite Pro (2% NSF + 5% nHA) twice daily | Varnish quarterly; dietary review; sealants | 6-monthly; QLF / ICDAS scoring |
| High Risk / ECC | Nanion Elite Pro (3% NSF + 5% nHA) — first-line | SDF 38% for cavitated; varnish quarterly; xylitol programme | 3-monthly; ICDAS, microhardness monitoring |
| Ortho / WSL | Elite Pro + targeted WSL fingertip application | Varnish at each ortho check-up; CPP-ACP adjunct | Each appointment; photo documentation |
| Xerostomia | Elite Pro — first-line (compensates absent saliva) | Saliva substitutes; xylitol lozenges; varnish monthly | Monthly during episode; 3-monthly otherwise |
| Sensitivity + Caries | Lite Pro or Elite Pro (nHA provides tubule occlusion) | Avoid SDF if aesthetics priority; CPP-ACP for Ca²⁺ | 6–8 weeks for sensitivity; NRS pain scale |

CAREGIVER EDUCATION

## Chair-Side Communication Framework

Clinical outcomes are heavily dependent on correct caregiver technique

#### Why no rinsing?

"This toothpaste contains two special ingredients — tiny silver particles that fight cavity-causing bacteria, and nano-hydroxyapatite, which is exactly the same material as your child's own tooth enamel. If you rinse, you wash these away before they have a chance to work. The protective film works for up to 12 hours. Spitting without rinsing is the most important thing you can do."

#### Why fingertip application to white spots?

"These white marks are early cavities forming under the surface. Putting a small amount directly on them with a clean finger — and leaving it there — allows the nano-hydroxyapatite to fill in porous areas and the silver to stop the bacteria making them worse. This is the equivalent of giving the tooth a direct treatment every day at home."

#### Is the silver safe?

"Yes. The silver is encapsulated — held in a protective shell that only releases where it needs to work, on the bacterial cells causing decay. It does not absorb into the body and won't stain the teeth black like some silver treatments applied in the clinic."

#### How is this different from regular toothpaste?

"Regular toothpaste leaves a protective layer on the outside. This toothpaste does that too, but it also kills the bacteria causing the cavity, breaks down the plaque shield, and fills in the early cavity from both inside and outside simultaneously. For a child with cavity history, this covers all four ways we need to protect the teeth."

## Safety Profile — PRO Dual-Matrix

### nHA Safety: Systemic and Local

Nano-hydroxyapatite is compositionally identical to the body's own bone and tooth mineral. It is non-cytotoxic at dentifrice concentrations, does not accumulate systemically (metabolised via normal calcium and phosphate pathways), and does not stain teeth, gingiva, or restorations. For paediatric patients, the nHA component raises no additional safety concerns.

### No Tooth Staining — Unlike SDF

SDF's black staining arises from free Ag⁺ reduction by sulphur-containing proteins in carious dentine. In Nanion Pro, AgNPs are chitosan-stabilised and do not release free Ag⁺ at concentrations sufficient to cause this reaction. Pro can be recommended for anterior teeth and aesthetically sensitive sites without the staining caveat that limits SDF use.

### Systemic Silver Safety in PRO Context

The addition of nHA does not alter the silver nanoparticle safety profile. Chitosan stabilisation of 5–8 nm AgNPs maintains colloidal structure preventing free ionic silver dissociation. Nanion Pro remains a rinse-off topical product with negligible systemic AgNP bioavailability.

### Safety & Caution

- • For ages 6 and above. Use under adult supervision for children.
- • Children 3–5: Elite Pro only under dentist guidance in confirmed high-ECC-risk cases.
- • Do not swallow. Keep out of reach of children.
- • Discontinue use if irritation occurs and consult a dentist.
- • Not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.
